conventions.arithmetic: exact integers; a probability is a reduced integer fraction; equality x/y = u/v is decided by x*v = u*y; no floating point anywhere in the verdict path
conventions.probability_encoding: string matching ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(/[1-9][0-9]*)?$ in lowest terms; denominator omitted only when 1; a JSON number in a probability field is a schema violation
conventions.state_encoding: s = v + n*h with v = s mod n the visible value and h = s div n the hidden value; n = |C_V|, m = |C_H|
conventions.orbit_representative: the least state index in the orbit; orbits listed in increasing representative
conventions.row_order: rows and columns of every matrix are visible values 0..n-1; a matrix is a map from row (decimal string) to a list of n probability strings
conventions.first_mismatch: the lexicographically least (a, j), a a visited row, j in 0..n-1, with T_alpha(a,j) != T_beta(a,j)
conventions.ell_min_rule: ell_min = n + 1; an orbit is long iff its length >= ell_min
conventions.pdiv: PDivisible N Gamma of CausalReadback.lean:54 on the stated row set; alpha: rows V_O, N = |O|; beta: rows C_V, N = ord(phi); computed by Lemma PD (Gamma_1 is a permutation matrix) on every instance and also by exact definitional feasibility on every toy control
conventions.verdicts: FREQ | NOT | VOID_NO_ORBIT per instance (PREREG-C1.md section 4.1)

wave_rule.step: for every site i, simultaneously: prev'_i = cur_i; cur'_i = (cur_{i-1} + cur_{i+1} - prev_i) mod q, indices mod L
wave_rule.region: R = {0, ..., r-1}; visible = the (prev, cur) pairs on R, n = q^(2r); hidden = the pairs off R, m = q^(2(L-r)); so v = s mod n and h = s div n
wave_rule.implementations: (i) the site loop above; (ii) the linear map F = [[0, I], [-I, A]] on (prev, cur) in (Z/q)^(2L), A the circulant ring adjacency; both must agree on every state of S

instances.rule: the wave rule with the -prev term deleted: prev'_i = cur_i; cur'_i = (cur_{i-1} + cur_{i+1}) mod q

instances.note: inputs to the comparator are parsed as integer fractions and reduced; '2/6' and '0/5' are comparator inputs, not output encodings
